pr_title: Bugfix iptables --random-fully must supported by kernel
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
> Uncomment only one ` /kind <>` line, hit enter to put that in a new line, and remove leading whitespace from that line:

/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
When kubernetes upgrade to v1.17 there are many network problems happened(as in the fixes issue list below).
I think the reason is, in the image of kube-proxy at kubernetes v1.17 the iptables is upgrade to 1.18, and the kube-proxy will add --random-fully at iptables Chain KUBE-POSTROUTING, but the "--random-fullly" only supported when kernel >= 1.13.  When kernel < 1.13 will happened those network problems.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

So, I've checked the pre-3.13 kernel source now, and passing `--random-fully` should have absolutely no effect. It will just set a bit in the flags in one of the data structures passed to the kernel, which the kernel will then just never notice because it doesn't look at that bit pre-3.13.

It seems that most of the reports linked above are on RHEL/CentOS 7. The RHEL 7 kernel is originally based on 3.10, but it has actually had full `--random-fully` support for a while. Thus, the problem is _not_ that we are passing `--random-fully` but shouldn't be. It's that either `--random-fully` is broken in general, or else that `--random-fully` is specifically broken on RHEL 7. (A few of the reports are from non-RHEL-7 users though, so...)

Or possibly (I don't yet understand all the details of the vxlan offload bug), "using `--random-fully` causes UDP packets to be more likely to hit the codepaths that result in bad checksums, for some reason, and maybe this is extra likely on RHEL 7, for some reason"

see this, @kuramal   the  kernel pr 
https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/ea64d8d6c675c0bb712689b13810301de9d8f77a
it mean  if  the udp header's check sum is  not 0, will do checksum

> So, I've checked the pre-3.13 kernel source now, and passing `--random-fully` should have absolutely no effect. It will just set a bit in the flags in one of the data structures passed to the kernel, which the kernel will then just never notice because it doesn't look at that bit pre-3.13.
> 
> It seems that most of the reports linked above are on RHEL/CentOS 7. The RHEL 7 kernel is originally based on 3.10, but it has actually had full `--random-fully` support for a while. Thus, the problem is _not_ that we are passing `--random-fully` but shouldn't be. It's that either `--random-fully` is broken in general, or else that `--random-fully` is specifically broken on RHEL 7. (A few of the reports are from non-RHEL-7 users though, so...)

I did some test case:
Case1:
```
OS: CentOS 7
kubernetes: 1.17.3
kernel:  3.10
host: iptable 1.4
pod of kube-proxy:  iptable 1.8

In this situation， --random-fully will enabled
Result:
Test Failed (means the network problem happen)
```
Case2:
```
Everything is the same with Case1, but disable --random-fully by update the kube-proxy code
Result:
Test OK (means the network works fine)
```
Case3:
```
Everything is the same with Case1, but update kernel to 4.4 by yum
In this situation， --random-fully will enabled
Result:
Test OK
```
Although I don't know how --random-fully affects the kernel, but from the test results, --random-fully should have absolutely effects.
And the man page of [iptables](https://manpages.debian.org/unstable/iptables/iptables-extensions.8.en.html) says the --random-fully working with kernel >= 3.13. I think it is necessary to check the kernel version before use --random-fully.

> Although I don't know how --random-fully affects the kernel, but from the test results, --random-fully should have absolutely effects.

Right. Not passing `--random-fully` makes the bug go away, but the problem isn't "RHEL 7's kernel doesn't support `--random-fully`". The problem is "RHEL 7's kernel supports `--random-fully`, but it's buggy". If you actually had a version of RHEL 7 that was old enough that it didn't have the `--random-fully` feature backported, then things would work whether or not you passed `--random-fully`.

(I'm not sure exactly what RHEL 7 release `--random-fully` showed up in. 7.0 doesn't have it, but 7.6 does.)

Notably, this PR won't help everyone, because some of the reporters are seeing this problem on newer kernels, so they'd still be getting `--random-fully` even with this PR. eg, the OP on #86507 has kernel 4.15.0.

There are definitely a lot more reports with RHEL/CentOS 7 users than with kernel 4.x users, and I'm not sure why. (We also don't know why this interacts with the VXLAN offload bug in the first place.)

**What happened**:

A question, are you 'curl'ing' from inside the Pod or from outside?

What happens here is that kube-proxy creates a Nat rule into the node, with the needed rule when it arrives into the Node.
